title: BBQ Chicken Bowls
shortDescription: Built bowls, big flavor, one line
subtitle: Built bowls, big flavor, one line
description: Built bowls, big flavor, one line. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Rinse and cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse long-grain rice until water runs clear. Simmer with a 1:1.5 rice-to-water ratio and a pinch of salt 18 minutes until tender. Fluff with a fork and hold covered at 200°F — dry rice won't accept sauce on the line.

steps.title: Season the chicken thighs
steps.instruction: Pat boneless chicken thighs dry; coat all over with BBQ rub. Let sit 10 minutes while the grill heats — dry skin chars instead of steaming.

steps.title: Grill chicken to 165°F
steps.instruction: Grill over medium-high 5–7 minutes per side until char marks show and thickest part reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Rest 5 minutes tented with foil — carryover finishes the last degrees.

steps.title: Slice rested chicken
steps.instruction: Slice chicken into strips against any grain you see. Hold in a hotel pan with a light glaze of warmed BBQ sauce spooned over — not drowned, or the line goes soggy.

steps.title: Dress the slaw
steps.instruction: Toss coleslaw mix with a splash of vinegar, salt, and pepper — keep cold on ice. Cold crunch against hot chicken is the bowl's texture contrast.

steps.title: Warm the corn
steps.instruction: Heat corn kernels in a dry skillet or on the grill 4–5 minutes until lightly charred and steaming. Season with salt; hold beside the rice.

steps.title: Warm the BBQ sauce
steps.instruction: Warm BBQ sauce in a small pot over low heat — do not boil or sugars scorch. Keep a ladle on the line for crews who want extra smoke on their bowl.

steps.title: Stage the bowl line
steps.instruction: Set rice in the first hotel pan, sliced chicken in the second, corn and slaw in separate pans. Hot components closest to the crew; cold slaw at the far end so it stays crisp.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.instruction: Base of rice, sliced BBQ chicken, charred corn, and a pile of slaw on top. Drizzle extra sauce on the side. BBQ Chicken Bowls move fastest when everyone can see all components before they grab a bowl.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover sliced chicken — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool sliced chicken and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Glaze sauce at the end so it doesn't burn on the grill.
Keep slaw on ice under the counter — warm slaw collapses in minutes.
Pull chicken at 163°F if holding under foil; verify 165°F before the line opens.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Log hold times on the pan with a grease pencil when tones drop mid-service.
Spot-check proteins with an instant-read thermometer before reopening the line after a call.
tonightSpread: Sides: steamed rice, charred corn, crunchy coleslaw
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.

leftovers: Cool sliced chicken in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.

whyCrewsLikeIt: Built bowls, big flavor, one line. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
